observations: A solid black cat-shaped form sits upright at center, its body covered with a white grid of crossing lines and a magenta vertical stripe running through the torso.
The head carries layered marks: teal ear fills, a yellow spiral, a white flower shape over one eye socket, and small white teeth visible along the open jaw.

The background divides into broad blue brushed rectangles upper-left, red structural shapes lower-right, and loose yellow and red vertical strokes lower-left, with a blue-and-yellow repeating wave band crossing the lower third.
reading: A black figure holds the center while the space around it refuses to settle — blue washes, red scaffolding, and scattered marks compete for the same ground. The white grid drawn across the body reads as containment or inventory, yet the magenta stripe and flower-eye push against any sense of order. The wave band at the bottom anchors nothing; it keeps moving.
contextAngle: Within the owned nnotb subset, title neighbors nnxyz nnotb #245 and nnxyz nnotb #247 share a cat-form motif but differ in palette weight: #245 works on a pale ground with close-up detail, #247 opens into warm yellow atmosphere. This work sits between those two moods.

connections.reason: Both center a cat-eared form with layered eye marks and looping line detail, but #245 fills the frame with a pale close-up face while #246 pulls back to show a full seated body against a busy multi-zone field.
Both place a cat-form against a multi-zone background with a horizontal band near the bottom, but #247 dissolves into warm yellow atmosphere where #246 keeps hard red and blue blocks.

lookingQuestion: Where does your eye go first — the grid drawn across the black body, the flower-and-spiral eye, or the wave band crossing the lower third — and what does that path tell you about how the marks are weighted?
ambiguities: The white grid on the torso could be a drawn texture or a reference to a specific object; the image alone does not resolve this.
nnxyz nifty faces #60 shares looping line density but its red-dominant palette and full-frame face structure offer no strong formal anchor to #246, so it was not selected as a connection.
